title: S3: a failed setup must not stop Orca from starting
description:
scripts/container/entrypoint.sh:230 calls die() when setup.sh fails, and die() exits. On the built-image path setup.sh is a VERIFICATION pass -- every phase reports 'already present' -- so its failure says something is wrong with the image, not that there is nothing to run. Killing the container there removes the only thing that could report the problem: no Orca, no terminal, no Claude Code.

Demote it: record the failure (run/provision/setup.status plus the existing setup.log), warn, and carry on to the privilege drop and orca-ide --serve. The one case that stays fatal is an ORCA_BIN that is not executable, because there is then genuinely nothing to serve -- and that check already exists at entrypoint.sh:618.

This is the smallest slice in the epic and the one that unblocks the rest: every later slice depends on the agent being able to see its own environment fail.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/container-entrypoint.bats
PASS-IF: with a setup.sh stub that exits 1, the entrypoint still writes run/orca-web-url.txt and still starts the Orca process; run/provision/setup.status contains a non-zero status; the run log carries the warning and NOT a die; with ORCA_BIN not executable the entrypoint still exits non-zero.
FROZEN: scripts/container/entrypoint.sh
CLASS: startup

title: S2 the card itself: card-update writes it with haiku, card-view draws it without scrolling
description:
scripts/card-update.sh -- the Stop hook's worker. Reads the hook JSON on stdin and takes .transcript_path (or a path as $1). Walks the transcript's user/assistant entries, skips isSidechain, drops thinking blocks, flattens text blocks and tool_use blocks to 'name + command/file_path/description', keeps the tail under a byte budget with a per-row cap so one runaway message cannot fill it. Sends that to 'claude -p --model ${CARD_MODEL:-claude-haiku-4-5-20251001}' with a prompt that fixes the shape -- NOW / WHY / DONE (up to 3) / NEXT / SNAG, at most 12 lines, no line over 68 characters, no preamble -- and writes the result to .claude-dev/run/card.md through a temp file and mv, so the viewer never reads half a card.

scripts/card-view.sh -- runs inside the pane. Clears and repaints; never appends, so the pane cannot scroll. Redraws on a change to the card file's mtime and on SIGWINCH, and otherwise sleeps. Clips every line to the pane width and the card to the pane height. Hides the cursor and restores it on exit.

Both fail open: no payload, no transcript, no jq, no model, a model that returns nothing -- exit 0 and leave the previous card alone.

CHECK: bats tests/card-render.bats
PASS-IF: the TAP output has the plan line '1..6', zero lines beginning 'not ok', and one 'ok' line for each of these six case names, verbatim:

  card-update exits 0 and leaves the previous card in place when there is no transcript or the model returns nothing

title: S1 card control: bin/card on|off|toggle|status|autostart, anchored to this terminal's own pane
description:
scripts/card.sh + bin/card (symlink, like bin/lane -> ../scripts/lane.sh).

Resolves the terminal it is running in: ORCA_PANE_KEY is '<tabId>:<leafId>'; match the leafId against 'orca terminal list --json' to get the handle. 'card on' splits that handle vertically running card-view, renames the new pane 'CARD', and records the handle in .claude-dev/run/card.pane and 'on' in .claude-dev/run/card.state. 'card off' closes the recorded pane and records 'off'. 'card toggle' flips. 'card status' prints one line. 'card autostart' is the SessionStart entry: open a pane when the state is on OR unset (default on), do nothing when it is off, and never open a second one when the recorded pane is still live.

Fails open, always: no ORCA_PANE_KEY, no orca CLI, an unreachable runtime, a stale handle -- each is 'exit 0, say so on one line', never an error that could stop a session starting.

  card autostart opens a pane when the state is on or unset and stays quiet when it is off

description: User rule (2026-09-06): 'my data never gets routed to China', built into the template; default stack Fable orchestrator + most capable GLM executor. Design: (1) config/provider-policy.json — default-deny allowlist of OpenRouter provider slugs with a country comment each (US/EU hosts only: deepinfra, together, fireworks, baseten, crusoe, coreweave, digitalocean, nebius, mistral, amazon-bedrock, venice, cerebras, groq, lambda, hyperbolic, parasail, google-vertex, azure — verify each slug against https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/<model>/endpoints 'tag' prefixes), an explicit denied list with the reason (z-ai, baidu, alibaba, siliconflow, streamlake: China; novita, atlas-cloud, gmicloud, phala, chutes, inceptron, ambient: unverifiable hosting -> denied by default), data_collection deny, allow_fallbacks false. (2) scripts/container/openrouter-guard.py (python3 stdlib, no deps): listens on 127.0.0.1:4141, reads the real key from OPENROUTER_API_KEY at start and the policy file; for POST /api/v1/chat/completions, /api/v1/completions, /api/v1/responses, /api/v1/messages it parses JSON, sets body.provider = {only: allowlist, allow_fallbacks: false, data_collection: 'deny'} (a client-supplied provider.order is kept only when every entry is in the allowlist; anything else is dropped and logged), forwards to https://openrouter.ai with the real key, streams SSE back; GET paths proxied; refuses any client key other than the guard token with 401; appends one line per request {ts, model, providers_forced, client_order_dropped} to <project>/.claude-dev/run/openrouter-guard.log. Clients receive OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<guard token> and base URL http://127.0.0.1:4141/api/v1, never the real key. (3) config/opencode/opencode.json provider.openrouter.options.baseURL = the guard URL (apiKey stays {env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY} which is the token in agent terminals); scripts/delegate.sh's opencode/codex openrouter paths use the guard URL too. (4) tier default: with an OpenRouter key present (file .claude-dev/home/.openrouter.key or env), '/tier <top>' derives worker = {orca, opencode, openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3} and recon stays subagent haiku, checker inherit; without a key the previous claude rung; '/tier worker claude:<x>' still overrides; tier-prime shows it. title: orca-launch: Orca uses the real ~/Library/Application Support (Electron ignores HOME on macOS) -> singleton lock EPERM, instant exit; pass --user-data-dir under a short per-project root
description: Why: on the user's Mac (2026-09-06) Orca.app exits immediately. orca-launch.log: readlink/create /Users/joerayment/Library/Application Support/orca/SingletonLock -> Operation not permitted, then Orca's own '[single-instance] Another Orca instance is already running' and exit; repo add times out waiting for orca-runtime.json. Root cause, verified from the extracted 1.4.197 bundle (out/main/index.js ~6808-6832): packaged Orca never calls app.setPath('userData'); Electron's appData on macOS comes from NSSearchPath, which ignores $HOME; and kei() then overwrites process.env.ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH with app.getPath('userData'), so our env var is discarded too. The Seatbelt profile denies /Users, so every write to the real Application Support fails, the lock first. Verified fix on the Linux build here (orca-linux-arm64.AppImage under Xvfb): with --user-data-dir=<dir>, SingletonLock, orca-runtime.json and the unix socket all landed in <dir> and nothing under ~/.config/orca -- Electron honors the switch natively, before Orca's lock. Second latent failure (claude-orca-qt9.10 part 1): the folder's userData path is ~90 bytes, plus o-<pid>-<4>.sock exceeds macOS's 104-byte sockaddr_un limit, so the transport would fail next. What: scripts/sandbox/orca-launch (1) host-side before sandbox-exec, creates a short per-project root: Darwin /private/tmp/co-<first 8 hex of sha1(project)>, elsewhere /tmp/co-<hash>, as a symlink to <project>/.claude-dev/home; refreshes it if it points elsewhere; refuses (exit 2, clear message) if the path exists and is not our symlink; CLAUDE_ORCA_SHORT_ROOT overrides the root. (2) exports ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<short root>/Library/Application Support/orca, mkdir -p the real dir, and passes --user-data-dir=<that path> as the first argument to the Orca binary. (3) refuses with a clear message when ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH length + 20 exceeds 100. (4) --print-command prints the exact env exports and sandbox-exec command line and exits 0 without launching, generating a profile, creating the symlink, or requiring sandbox-exec; --print-env prints just the exports. HOME and TMPDIR stay as they are. gen-orca-profile.sh needs no change: /private/tmp is readable and writes through the symlink resolve into the project.
design: Env knobs: CLAUDE_ORCA_SHORT_ROOT (override the short root, used by tests to force a too-long path), existing CLAUDE_ORCA_METADATA_TIMEOUT. Alternatives rejected: ORCA_BYPASS_SINGLE_INSTANCE_LOCK=1 (only skips the first casualty; the data dir is still denied); ORCA_E2E_USER_DATA_DIR (works but flips Orca's E2E mode on); a profileExceptions write-allow on the real Application Support (leaks Orca state outside the folder and makes every project share one lock). Supersedes part (1) of claude-orca-qt9.10; its dark-mode and doctor parts stay there. Mac behaviour (Seatbelt resolving the symlink into the project) is unverifiable here; the test proves the argv/env/symlink logic with a stub sandbox-exec.

title: V6 First-real-run fixes: short HOME symlink for Orca's socket, dark-mode default, doctor socket check (verified with the Linux Orca)
description:
Why: the first real Orca run (Linux AppImage in this container, with the folder's .claude-dev/home as HOME) exposed one blocker and one preference. Blocker: Orca's daemon socket lives under the user-data dir derived from HOME, and a deep project path pushes it past the sockaddr_un limit (108 bytes on Linux, 104 on macOS) — Orca shows "couldn't start its local command transport… path is too long", the CLI becomes unavailable, and our launch-time `repo add` and the opt-in orchestration mode silently break. A short symlink to the same home directory (e.g. /tmp/oh → <project>/.claude-dev/home) fixed it. Preference: the user wants the sandboxed Orca in dark mode by default.
What: (1) scripts/sandbox/orca-launch creates, host-side before launch, a short per-project symlink to <project>/.claude-dev/home under a short root — Darwin: /private/tmp/co-<8 hex of sha1(project)> (readable in layer 1, never writable by layer 1 or 2; the symlink target resolves into the project so the profile's project rules apply); Linux: /tmp/co-<hash> — refreshes it if it points elsewhere, refuses (exit 2) if the path exists and is not our symlink, and exports HOME=<symlink> (TMPDIR and ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH stay as they are); it also computes the expected socket path length and refuses with a clear message when it would still exceed 100 bytes. `orca-launch --print-env` prints the exact env it would use (for the Linux demo and tests) and `--print-command` the sandbox-exec command line. (2) claude-dev --doctor warns when the socket path for the folder would exceed 100 bytes without the symlink and shows the symlink in the Orca section. (3) Dark mode: registration pre-seeds Orca's global settings file in the in-folder user-data dir (find the key and file from src/shared/global-settings-types.ts and src/main/global-settings* in the Orca clone; write only when the file is absent so a user's later choice is never overwritten) with the dark theme; the seed writes both the macOS location (Library/Application Support/orca/…) and the Linux one (.config/orca/…) under <project>/.claude-dev/home so either build picks it up; `sandbox.json` `orca.theme` (dark|light|system, default dark) selects it. (4) The Linux demo becomes the verification: launch the AppImage with `orca-launch --print-env`'s environment (no bypass switches added to the product; on Linux orca-launch itself refuses to launch because sandbox-exec is absent — the demo uses the printed env), confirm Orca starts in dark mode with the CLI transport working (no "path too long" modal), `repo add` succeeds, and screenshot it.
Boundaries: no profile content changes beyond none needed (the symlink target resolves into the project); no docs beyond README's sandbox.json options line for orca.theme and a knowledge-base note on the socket limit.
design: Evidence from the Linux run: socket path limit hit with HOME=<project>/.claude-dev/home; /tmp/oh symlink fixed it; user data at <HOME>/.config/orca; orca-runtime.json lists the unix socket and ws://127.0.0.1:6768; Linux CLI binary is resources/bin/orca-ide (macOS: Contents/Resources/bin/orca). Keep bash 3.2 lint clean; PASS-IF names verbatim as @test names; dry-run assertions before RED.

title: V2d Wrapper writes under layer 1: srt settings to a private per-launch temp dir agents cannot write; config-hash to run/
description:
Why: the wrapper (claude-orca-shell) and config-sync run INSIDE layer 1 when Orca launches a terminal, and layer 1 write-denies .claude-dev/state (host-owned). Two wrapper outputs still target it: the srt settings file state/srt-<sha1>.json and config-sync's state/config-hash. On the Mac every Orca terminal would fail to start (settings unwritable) or re-sync every time. The settings file is also security-sensitive: it defines layer 2, so it must not be written anywhere an agent (layer 2) can write — .claude-dev/run and tmp are agent-writable and an agent could race the wrapper between write and exec.
What: claude-orca-shell writes the srt settings file to a private per-launch directory that layer 1 allows and layer 2 denies: on Darwin `mktemp -d "$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)/claude-orca.XXXXXX"` (under /private/var/folders, which the Orca profile allows and srt's allowWrite never includes), mode 700, file mode 600, removed by an EXIT trap after exec is unreachable — or kept for srt to read: srt reads the file at startup before sandboxing, so the wrapper writes, execs srt, and the directory is cleaned by the next launch (document); elsewhere `mktemp -d`. config-sync's checksum moves to run/config-hash (the hash only gates re-sync; an agent tampering with it can only force or skip a sync, powers it already has via the config dir). gen-settings/gen-orca-profile: document which paths each layer writes. Tests in tests/wrapper-writes.bats (frozen) with the named cases; update tests/config-sync.bats / sandbox-config.bats / selftest.bats paths (unfrozen).
Boundaries: no probe additions (V3), no docs (V5).
design: Layer-1 allowed write roots per gen-orca-profile.sh: <project>, /private/var/folders, /dev. Layer 2 (srt) allowWrite: project-scoped only, so /private/var/folders is agent-denied. getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR returns /var/folders/xx/.../T/ on macOS; absent on Linux (fall back to mktemp -d). Keep bash 3.2 lint clean.

title: S2b Shell-entry hardening: bash 3.2 compatibility, non-interactive login shells, rc block placement
description:
Why: three findings from S2's verification and the real install run must be closed before the wrapper is trusted on a Mac. (1) macOS /bin/bash is 3.2: `arr+=("${empty[@]}")` under `set -u` aborts there, so gen-settings.sh (and any sibling script with the same idiom) would fail closed on every Mac shell whenever extraAllowWrite is empty — every script under scripts/ must run under bash 3.2. (2) Non-interactive login shells (`zsh -l -c …`, `bash -l -c …`) do not read .zshrc/.bashrc, so they start unsandboxed inside a bootstrapped folder; Orca's agent terminals are interactive and covered, but the hook must also live in .zprofile/.bash_profile-login path and preserve the -c command through the re-exec (zsh: $ZSH_EXECUTION_STRING; bash: $BASH_EXECUTION_STRING). (3) rc-install must append its block LAST (after Homebrew shellenv lines) and the bash side must cover .bash_profile and .profile-less setups consistently.

What: scripts/sandbox/* and scripts/launcher.sh rc-install made bash-3.2-safe (guard idiom `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}`, no associative arrays, no mapfile, no ${var,,}); shellrc.zsh/.bash re-exec that carries the execution string: `exec claude-orca-shell --root R -- zsh -l -c "$ZSH_EXECUTION_STRING"` when set (bash likewise), interactive re-exec unchanged; claude-orca-shell accepts a trailing `-c <cmd>` for the inner shell; rc-install writes the marker block into ~/.zprofile as well as ~/.zshrc (both guarded by CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED so the second source is a no-op), keeps ~/.bash_profile, and always appends after existing content; tests/helpers/ensure_bash32 builds GNU bash 3.2.57 into tests/.cache/bash32 (from the scratchpad copy at /tmp/claude-1000/-workspace/7037bfad-67da-4b5e-9adb-944b260fc264/scratchpad/bash32/install when present, else from ftp.gnu.org) so the suite can run the scripts under the real macOS bash version.

Boundaries: no self-test probes (S3), no config sync (S4). tests/sandbox-config.bats and tests/bootstrap.bats are unfrozen (S1/S2 closed) and must stay green; add cases there only if a premise changed.
design: Findings source: verifier report on claude-orca-3sk.14 (bash 3.2 `+=` under set -u; rc residue) and the orchestrator's install run (non-interactive -c shells bypass .zshrc). Real bash 3.2 for tests: GNU bash-3.2.57 built with gcc (build-essential is present); cache under tests/.cache/bash32 (gitignored). The wrapper's stub srt in tests must record the full inner command so the "-c preserved" cases can assert it verbatim.

title: S2 Sandbox wrapper: srt settings generator, scope derivation, env, shell re-exec, fail-closed
description:
Why: the security core. Every shell opened in a bootstrapped folder (by Orca, Terminal.app, or `orca terminal create`) must re-exec itself inside srt/sandbox-exec with a scope derived from the folder, before any agent binary runs.

What: ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-root (primary checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, falls back to walking up for .claude-dev/sandbox.json), ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-shell (generates srt settings, sets env, `exec srt --settings <file> -c 'exec zsh -l'`), shellrc.zsh + shellrc.bash (sourced from the user's rc via one marker-delimited line installed/removed idempotently by `claude-dev`), scripts/sandbox/gen-settings.sh (pure function: inputs → JSON).

Scope: primary session allowWrite=[<project>, <project>/.claude-dev/home, <project>/.claude-dev/tmp]; linked worktree session allowWrite=[<worktree>, <primary>/.git, <primary>/.beads, <primary>/.claude-dev/home, <primary>/.claude-dev/tmp]. denyRead=[real HOME]; allowRead=[<project>, <worktree>, ~/.claude-orca, ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.orca/agent-hooks]. Extra denyWrite (host-executed files): orca.yaml, .worktreeinclude, .envrc, .beads/hooks/**. network.allowedDomains = defaults ∪ validated sandbox.json extras; strictAllowlist true; allowLocalBinding true; allowPty true; enableWeakerNetworkIsolation true; allowAppleEvents false; allowUnixSockets [] (S9 may add the Orca runtime dir). Env inside: HOME=<primary>/.claude-dev/home, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude, TMPDIR=<primary>/.claude-dev/tmp, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GH_CONFIG_DIR, BEADS_DIR=<primary>/.beads, ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_REAL_HOME, PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:<real ~>/.local/bin:~/.claude-orca/template/bin:...

Fail closed: srt or sandbox-exec missing, generator error, or unvalidated sandbox.json → the shellrc defines refusing functions for claude, codex, gemini, opencode and prints the reason; never continue unsandboxed silently.

Boundaries: no auth/credential masking config beyond the hook point (S5), no Orca hook merge (S6), no self-test (S3). The wrapper treats everything under <project> as untrusted data.
design: gen-settings.sh is a pure bash function taking (primary, worktree, real_home, sandbox_json, mode) and printing JSON via jq so tests can assert exact documents. Settings file path: <primary>/.claude-dev/state/srt-<sha1(worktree)>.json. Schema validation test uses `node -e` importing the installed sandbox-runtime package (stub-installed in tests from the scratchpad clone or npm cache; skip with a clear reason only if node is absent). Real srt facts used: deny default; writes allow-only; allowLocalBinding opens localhost outbound; allowPty for /dev/ttys*; mandatory write-denies under cwd for shell rc files, .mcp.json, .claude/agents, .claude/commands, .git/hooks, .git/config (srt src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:15-40, macos-sandbox-utils.ts:79-106).

title: S3 Sandbox self-test and claude-dev --doctor (13 probes, bootstrap gate)
description:
Why: the sandbox must be proven from the inside on the Mac, automatically, before Orca ever launches an agent — the Linux container cannot run sandbox-exec. This turns "verify on the Mac" into a product feature instead of a to-do.

What: scripts/sandbox/selftest.sh run by `claude-orca-shell --selftest` inside the sandbox; probes (single table = source of truth): write-outside-denied (touch under real HOME), read-real-home-denied (ls ~/.ssh), keychain-denied (security find-generic-password), project-writable, worktree-writable, sibling-worktree-denied, tmp-outside-denied (/private/tmp), network-blocked-domain (curl example.com), network-allowed-domain (curl api.anthropic.com any HTTP status), orca-socket-unreachable (orca status fails unless S9 mode), sandbox-exec-present, srt-version-pinned, git-hooks-audit (no .git/hooks/* references into the writable scope). Results JSON → <project>/.claude-dev/state/selftest.json with timestamp. `claude-dev --doctor` prints the table and exits 2 when selftest.json is absent, stale (>24h) or failed; `claude-dev` registration runs the self-test and refuses hand-off on failure. `SRT_DEBUG` capture of the generated profile saved to .claude-dev/state/ for audit.

design: Probe implementations are shell functions; the runner is testable on Linux by injecting a fake probe executor (CLAUDE_ORCA_SELFTEST_FAKE=<file mapping probe→exit code>). Doctor reuses the launcher's tool checks from S1.

title: S2 Sandbox wrapper: srt settings generator, scope derivation, env, shell re-exec, fail-closed
description:
Why: the security core. Every shell opened in a bootstrapped folder (by Orca, Terminal.app, or `orca terminal create`) must re-exec itself inside srt/sandbox-exec with a scope derived from the folder, before any agent binary runs.

What: ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-root (primary checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, falls back to walking up for .claude-dev/sandbox.json), ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-shell (generates srt settings, sets env, `exec srt --settings <file> -c 'exec zsh -l'`), shellrc.zsh + shellrc.bash (sourced from the user's rc via one marker-delimited line installed/removed idempotently by `claude-dev`), scripts/sandbox/gen-settings.sh (pure function: inputs → JSON).

Scope: primary session allowWrite=[<project>, <project>/.claude-dev/home, <project>/.claude-dev/tmp]; linked worktree session allowWrite=[<worktree>, <primary>/.git, <primary>/.beads, <primary>/.claude-dev/home, <primary>/.claude-dev/tmp]. denyRead=[real HOME]; allowRead=[<project>, <worktree>, ~/.claude-orca, ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.orca/agent-hooks]. Extra denyWrite (host-executed files): orca.yaml, .worktreeinclude, .envrc, .beads/hooks/**. network.allowedDomains = defaults ∪ validated sandbox.json extras; strictAllowlist true; allowLocalBinding true; allowPty true; enableWeakerNetworkIsolation true; allowAppleEvents false; allowUnixSockets [] (S9 may add the Orca runtime dir). Env inside: HOME=<primary>/.claude-dev/home, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude, TMPDIR=<primary>/.claude-dev/tmp, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GH_CONFIG_DIR, BEADS_DIR=<primary>/.beads, ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_REAL_HOME, PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:<real ~>/.local/bin:~/.claude-orca/template/bin:...

Fail closed: srt or sandbox-exec missing, generator error, or unvalidated sandbox.json → the shellrc defines refusing functions for claude, codex, gemini, opencode and prints the reason; never continue unsandboxed silently.

Boundaries: no auth/credential masking config beyond the hook point (S5), no Orca hook merge (S6), no self-test (S3). The wrapper treats everything under <project> as untrusted data.
design: gen-settings.sh is a pure bash function taking (primary, worktree, real_home, sandbox_json, mode) and printing JSON via jq so tests can assert exact documents. Settings file path: <primary>/.claude-dev/state/srt-<sha1(worktree)>.json. Schema validation test uses `node -e` importing the installed sandbox-runtime package (stub-installed in tests from the scratchpad clone or npm cache; skip with a clear reason only if node is absent). Real srt facts used: deny default; writes allow-only; allowLocalBinding opens localhost outbound; allowPty for /dev/ttys*; mandatory write-denies under cwd for shell rc files, .mcp.json, .claude/agents, .claude/commands, .git/hooks, .git/config (srt src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:15-40, macos-sandbox-utils.ts:79-106).

title: S5: the agent inside can see and repair its own provisioning
description:
'provision status' prints one row per step (name, ok/failed, when, the last line of its log) and 'provision run <step>' re-runs one. Both live in the template's bin/ like lane and tier-set, so they are typeable by name inside the container.

The session-start hook surfaces FAILED steps only -- a clean folder says nothing, a broken one puts the failing step and its last log line in front of the agent on the first prompt. That is the whole point of the epic: the environment reports its own faults to the thing that can fix them.

'claude-dev --doctor' on the Mac side grows the same rows, so a folder can be diagnosed from either side.

title: S4: provision.d -- the project-shaped work moves after Orca is serving
description:
Everything that is about THIS FOLDER rather than about the image comes out of the blocking path and becomes a numbered, idempotent step under scripts/container/provision.d/, run after orca-ide --serve has published its URL: toolchain verify (setup.sh --check), bd init, the instruction/config sync, orca repo add, git identity, the OpenRouter guard.

Each step writes run/provision/<step>.log and run/provision/<step>.status. No step is fatal. A step that fails leaves a status a human and an agent can both read, and the next start re-runs it -- idempotence is the whole contract, so every step must be safe to run on an already-provisioned folder.

The ordering constraint that made this necessary: the steps a folder needs are exactly the steps most likely to fail (a network hiccup, a half-written config, a bad token), and they were all in front of the thing that could have reported them.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/container-entrypoint.bats plus a new tests/provision.bats
PASS-IF: every file in provision.d runs twice in a row with the same final status (idempotence, asserted per step); a step that exits non-zero leaves its status file non-zero and does not stop later steps or the Orca process; the web URL is written BEFORE the first step runs.
FROZEN: scripts/container/provision.d/
CLASS: startup

title: S1: split the Dockerfile into claude-orca-base and the folder image
description:
Dockerfile.base carries the apt half (setup.sh --image) and the six payload phases (bats, dolt, bd, orca, opencode, claude) and builds the image claude-orca-base:<IMAGE_TAG>. Dockerfile becomes FROM claude-orca-base:<tag>, plus 'COPY --chown=agent:agent . /opt/claude-orca' and the template phase -- two layers.

acquire_image builds the base first when the daemon does not already hold it, then the folder image. A base that is present is never rebuilt implicitly: only --prebuild (S2) and a pin move rebuild it, because the base is the 15-minute half and nothing should pay it by surprise.

Pins stay in setup.sh; the ARG lines move to Dockerfile.base with them. .dockerignore already excludes .claude-dev, .git and tests/.cache -- the top image's context stays ~2 MB.

title: S2: claude-dev --prebuild, and an update that does not block on the base
description:
A command that builds or refreshes claude-orca-base without a folder waiting on it, so the 15-minute half is paid deliberately rather than by whoever registers next. --update builds the base in the background and leaves the folder on its current image until the new one is ready, so an update never stops the world -- the thing that just went wrong twice.

Reports the base image id before and after, the same way cmd_update_v3 already reports the folder image, so 'it did not move' is a sentence the output can say.

title: Two-image build, and a startup that cannot wall off the agent
description:
Two related changes, one cause. The image is now built on the machine that runs it (commit pending, this session): no CI, no registry, no token. This epic splits that build in two and moves everything project-shaped out of the blocking path.

MEASURED PAYLOAD (read off the live container, 2026-09-08): Orca 529M, Claude Code 206M, opencode 176M, bd 128M, dolt 114M, bats 0.1M -- ~1.15 GB that moves only when a pin moves, sitting under ~2 MB of repo that moves every push.

HONEST CORRECTION to the argument that opened this: the per-push chain is ALREADY short. Dockerfile:35 copies setup.sh on its own line above the six payload RUNs, and the repo copy is the last layer, so editing a script today invalidates only 'COPY . /opt/claude-orca' and the template phase. The split does NOT buy a cheaper push -- the layer order already did. What it buys is a base that can be built deliberately and early (prebuild/warm) instead of only as a side effect of someone's first register, insurance against a cold or pruned cache, and a clean seam if the base is ever worth publishing once a quarter.

THE OTHER HALF, which is the user's original ask and the more important one: scripts/container/entrypoint.sh:230 calls die() when setup.sh fails, which exits before Orca ever starts. A failing step 1 therefore removes the observer -- no Orca, no terminal, no Claude Code, and nothing inside that could report the failure. Features got built on top of a foundation nobody could see was broken. Orca must come up even when provisioning is broken, and the steps must be visible and re-runnable from inside.

title: Epic: an index-card panel beside Claude Code, written by a small model
description:
A pane next to the Claude Code terminal holding ONE index card -- what is happening, why, what is done, what is next, what is stuck. It never scrolls: the card is replaced, not appended. Opus writes long and buries the point; the card is written by haiku, which is the whole reason the feature exists.

MECHANISM (all of it verified on 2026-09-08 before this was written):
* Orca has no plugin, webview or custom-pane API -- its right sidebar is
  hardcoded (explorer/search/sourceControl/checks/ports) and plugins only
  contribute VM recipes. What it does have is
  'orca terminal split --terminal <handle> --direction vertical --command <cmd>',
  which puts an arbitrary program in a pane of the current tab. That is the panel.
* A terminal knows its own identity from the environment Orca sets:
  ORCA_PANE_KEY is '<tabId>:<leafId>', and leafId matches a row of
  'orca terminal list --json'. So a hook running inside the session can find the
  handle of the terminal it is running in, and split THAT one.
* Claude Code hook payloads carry .transcript_path (confirmed in the binary), and
  the transcript is JSONL of user/assistant entries whose content blocks are
  text / tool_use / thinking. Dropping thinking leaves a compact record of the turn.
* 'claude -p --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' answers in ~4s cold, ~47s for a
  6k-character transcript tail. It runs from the Stop hook, backgrounded, so it
  can never make a turn wait.

SHAPE:
  scripts/card.sh (bin/card)  on | off | toggle | status | autostart
  scripts/card-update.sh      Stop hook: transcript tail -> haiku -> run/card.md
  scripts/card-view.sh        runs IN the pane: clear, draw one boxed card, wait
  config/claude-commands/card.md   the /card slash command -- the control
  config/claude-settings.json      SessionStart -> card autostart (background)
                                   Stop         -> card update   (background)
  .claude-dev/run/card.state  on|off, default on   .claude-dev/run/card.pane  handle
                              .claude-dev/run/card.md  the card itself

THE CONTROL: /card toggles, /card on and /card off are explicit. One word to
remember, in the TUI the person is already typing in -- not a shell command that
would mean leaving the session.

EVERY PIECE FAILS OPEN. These run in hooks: no Orca, no jq, no model, no
transcript must each mean 'exit 0, no card', never a session that will not start.
close_reason: Closed

title: startup v4 S2b: supersedes qa2.10 -- the image no longer carries the toolchain, so 'which image' stopped being the same question as 'does this start install anything'; weburl_timeout needs both halves
design:
qa2.10 froze this file when 'which image is it' and 'does this start install anything' were the same question. The image now carries only apt (setup.sh IMAGE_PHASES); the toolchain -- Orca, Claude Code, opencode, bd, dolt, bats -- installs on a folder's first start into <project>/.claude-dev/toolchain, mounted over /usr/local, /opt/Orca and /opt/claude.

So the two questions came apart, in both directions: a PULLED image with an empty cache has ~5 minutes of toolchain to install, and a RUNTIME image reinstalls its apt half on every recreate however full that cache is (dpkg state cannot live in a bind mount). weburl_timeout now asks start_installs_nothing() -- cache populated AND image not runtime -- and only then waits 120s.

Measured on a real Mac (2026-09-07, Docker Desktop 29): keyed on the toolchain cache alone, a runtime-path recreate got 120s for a 280s job and the launcher gave up on a container that was working fine. The corrected case is red against the qa2.10 launcher (pulled + empty cache answers 120, must answer 1800) and green against this one.

Only case 5 changes. The other six are qa2.10's, unedited.

title: S6 Orca integration: managed hooks merge, statusline chain, sub-agent rows, transcript visibility
description:
Why: the point of Orca is seeing what agents do — working/waiting/done dots, sub-agent child rows, session history. Orca implements these through hooks it writes into the real ~/.claude/settings.json, which the sandboxed Claude (own config dir) never loads unless we carry them over.

What: the wrapper (host side, every launch) merges Orca's managed entries — identified by the ~/.orca/agent-hooks/claude-hook.sh command — for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TeammateIdle, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PostCompact from ~/.claude/settings.json into <config dir>/settings.json without duplicating ours; removes them when Orca's are gone; chains Orca's claude-statusline.sh before our statusline; allowRead ~/.orca/agent-hooks (already in S2); ORCA_* env passes through untouched; Orca's curl uses --noproxy 127.0.0.1 and allowLocalBinding covers the POST. Transcript visibility: verify on the Mac whether Orca's session history / usage see $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects (Orca reads the env of its own process, not the agent's); if not, the wrapper writes a symlink ~/.claude/projects/<slug> → <config dir>/projects/<slug> (host side, outside the sandbox). Registration prints the one-time Settings → Repository worktree base path suggestion (<project>/.orca-worktrees).

title: claude_orca: port claude_docker to a macOS Seatbelt sandbox managed by Orca
description:
Port the claude_docker template to a macOS-native design: agents run under Apple's Seatbelt (sandbox-exec via Anthropic's pinned `srt` runtime) scoped to the project folder, and Orca (onorca.dev) manages sessions, worktrees, status and sub-agent rows. Keep beads, --dangerously-skip-permissions, /tier, and the hook/guard suite. Claude Code stays primary; Codex/Gemini/OpenCode run inside the same sandbox and take instructions from Claude. Drop the tmux fleet sidebar, worktree-sessions (cs-new/peers/session-title) and all Docker-bound machinery.

Plan with findings, design, risks and slice table: .claude/plans/orca-port.md (this repo). Source material: attachments/claude_docker (old template), Orca 1.4.197 and srt 0.0.75 sources (cloned during planning; refs in the plan).

Trust-boundary invariant every slice must respect: nothing that runs unsandboxed executes or sources anything agent-writable. Host-owned root is ~/.claude-orca (bin, template clone, srt, shellrc); project-owned root is <project>/ (including .claude-dev/{home,tmp,state,sandbox.json}). No ./claude-dev launcher lives in the project root; the launcher is `claude-dev` on PATH.

Verification split: this container is Linux. Each slice's CHECK is Linux-runnable (bats over the shell logic with srt/brew/gh/npm stubbed; schema validation against the pinned srt). Slices with macOS-only behaviour also carry a MAC-CHECK line naming the self-test that bootstrap runs on the Mac and refuses to hand over without; MAC-CHECK is informational for the verifier, never a reason to close.

GitHub: repo name claude_orca (beads prefix is already claude-orca). Creation from this session is blocked — the gh token cannot create repositories (GraphQL createRepository and REST POST /user/repos → 403). When joe-rayment/claude_orca exists: add it as origin and publish main.
close_reason: All slices S1–S12 (+S2b) implemented, independently verified under their acceptance contracts, and merged into main at 3d59e31; ./run-tests.sh 673 ok; bead-auditor held all 13 active closures. Open follow-ups recorded in .claude/plans/orca-port.md §8 (Mac self-test run, gh-token masking default, --prompt-file coverage).

What: bootstrap.sh (curl|bash via `gh api repos/joe-rayment/claude_orca/contents/bootstrap.sh -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" | bash`), scripts/launcher.sh installed as ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-dev (commands: register (default, cwd=project), --doctor, --update, --teardown, --uninstall — the last three are S12/S3 stubs here), Brewfile (git gh jq ripgrep node bats-core bd; no helix/tmux), scripts/install-tools.sh (brew bundle check/install, Orca cask presence → prints `brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca` if missing), scripts/install-srt.sh (`npm --prefix ~/.claude-orca/srt install @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime@0.0.75`, node >= 20.11 check), template clone into ~/.claude-orca/template, per-project registration: creates <project>/.claude-dev/{home,tmp,state}, sandbox.json defaults, seeds .gitignore (.claude-dev/, .mcp.json, attachments/, .claude/logs/), creates attachments/, prints "open this folder in Orca".

title: tier-hooks.bats 'no Orca' leg reads the live runtime and fails inside the container
description:
tests/tier-hooks.bats:546 runs 'tier_set opus' with no TIER_ORCA_PROBE_CMD and line 548 asserts .roles.worker.backend == "subagent". That only holds on a box with no reachable Orca. Inside the folder's own container -- now the normal place to run the suite -- orca-ide is up and tier_orca_reachable() returns true, so the backend derives as 'orca' and the case fails.

Proved: same tier-set.sh invocation, scratch CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT, OPENROUTER_API_KEY set, no key file:

title: Rebuild and republish the image so the Orca Web paste shim reaches folders
description:
patch-orca-web-theme.py now injects a second seed into the served web-index.html that hides navigator.clipboard.readText, which selects Orca's own native-paste fallback and makes Cmd+V work in a terminal with no browser permission. Verified end to end on this box against a real orca-ide --serve and a real Chromium: with the patched app.asar and clipboard-read in state 'prompt', Ctrl+V put an auth code at the shell prompt (attachments/orca-paste-verified.png).

The patch is applied by setup.sh phase_template, which the entrypoint runs at every container start -- but from TEMPLATE_ROOT, which is the BAKED /opt/claude-orca copy whenever the folder runs the prebuilt image. So an existing folder keeps the old script until a new image is built and made available; only the ubuntu:24.04 runtime path picks it up from the folder's own template clone.

Follow-up: build the image from this commit via .github/workflows/image.yml and make it the pinned IMAGE_TAG, then confirm on a Mac that a folder started on it pastes into a terminal without granting the Chrome Clipboard permission.

description: The entrypoint prefers /opt/claude-orca when it exists, so on the pulled path setup.sh, config/ and the entrypoint all come from the image. Editing <project>/.claude-dev/template on a pulled folder changes nothing inside the container. This is defensible (the image is the pinned artifact) and cheap to work with now that the repo COPY is the last Docker layer, but it is not written down anywhere a person would look, and it surprised this session. Decide: document it in the README, or make the folder's clone win when it is newer -- noting that the clone is agent-writable, so preferring it means the container's PID 1 executes agent-writable code as root.

title: OpenRouter guard: the real key is visible via ps/proc to any same-uid process while the guard runs (argv/environ), not just to the guard itself
description: Found by the qa2.21 verifier, does not affect that bead's PASS. entrypoint.sh starts the guard as 'env OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<real key> python3 <guard script> ...', so the key sits in that process's argv and /proc/<pid>/environ, readable by any process running as the same agent uid (e.g. a worker terminal doing ps -ef or reading /proc). The guard's whole purpose is to keep the key out of agent terminals' reach, so this is a real if narrow gap: an agent that specifically goes looking (ps -ef | grep OPENROUTER, or reads /proc/<guard-pid>/environ) can still recover the real key, though normal agent env/config never shows it. Fix: pass the key to the guard via a pipe/fd or a mode-600 file read once at startup instead of argv/env, and have the guard scrub it from its own os.environ immediately after reading (argv still needs care: use env -u or read from stdin instead of an argv assignment).

title: Orca Web opens in light mode; it should be dark
description: Seen in the 2026-09-06 live demo screenshots (attachments/demo-1..3): Orca Web renders light. seed-orca-state.sh writes settings.theme (CLAUDE_ORCA_THEME, default dark) into orca-data.json, but the v3-status memory already records 'Orca Web ignores settings.theme'. Find how Orca Web 1.4.197 chooses its theme (grep the extracted bundle under scratchpad/orca-asar/out/web and out/renderer for theme / prefers-color-scheme / localStorage keys / a settings RPC field the web client reads) and make the served UI dark by default: seed the right field (profile settings via 'settings.update' RPC from the entrypoint after 'Orca server ready', or a web-client default), verify with a real screenshot of the paired web UI (same method as the demo: playwright with a render wait) — closes on a viewed dark screenshot.

So orca-data.json settings.theme cannot darken the web UI. theme-1-asis.png: seeded dark on disk, served page html.class=light, body rgb(255,255,255). title: S9 Opt-in Orca orchestration mode (orca CLI socket inside the sandbox, skills, hardening checklist)
description:
Why: Orca's orchestration layer (runs, tasks, `orca orchestration worker-start --agent codex --worktree current`, messages, gates) is the most native way for Claude to direct other models and have Orca show every worker. But the orca CLI socket is a remote control for an unsandboxed app: `orca terminal create --command …` runs anything outside the sandbox unless the shell is in one of this project's worktrees, `orca goto/exec` drives an unsandboxed browser (network escape), automations and artifacts run outside too. So this is opt-in, off by default, and the residual surface is stated every time it is on.

What: <project>/.claude-dev/sandbox.json `{"orca": {"cli": true}}` → the wrapper adds allowUnixSockets [<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca] and allowRead of that dir, passes ORCA_CLI_COMMAND through, installs the orca-cli + orchestration skills into the config dir (from the Orca repo's skills/, pinned copy under template/), and adds a rulebook addendum: Claude is the coordinator; a tier's executor slice may become `orca orchestration worker-start --task <id> --worktree current --agent <codex|claude|gemini>` (same worktree → sandboxed by S2); workers report worker_done; beads remain the source of truth. `claude-dev --doctor` prints the escape-surface warning and the Orca settings to harden (Floating Workspace off, public artifact links off, no per-repo setup hooks) whenever the mode is on. The self-test's orca-socket probe expects reachable in this mode.

Boundaries: no attempt to sandbox Orca itself.

title: S9 Opt-in Orca orchestration mode (orca CLI socket inside the sandbox, skills, hardening checklist)
description:
Why: Orca's orchestration layer (runs, tasks, `orca orchestration worker-start --agent codex --worktree current`, messages, gates) is the most native way for Claude to direct other models and have Orca show every worker. But the orca CLI socket is a remote control for an unsandboxed app: `orca terminal create --command …` runs anything outside the sandbox unless the shell is in one of this project's worktrees, `orca goto/exec` drives an unsandboxed browser (network escape), automations and artifacts run outside too. So this is opt-in, off by default, and the residual surface is stated every time it is on.

What: <project>/.claude-dev/sandbox.json `{"orca": {"cli": true}}` → the wrapper adds allowUnixSockets [<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca] and allowRead of that dir, passes ORCA_CLI_COMMAND through, installs the orca-cli + orchestration skills into the config dir (from the Orca repo's skills/, pinned copy under template/), and adds a rulebook addendum: Claude is the coordinator; a tier's executor slice may become `orca orchestration worker-start --task <id> --worktree current --agent <codex|claude|gemini>` (same worktree → sandboxed by S2); workers report worker_done; beads remain the source of truth. `claude-dev --doctor` prints the escape-surface warning and the Orca settings to harden (Floating Workspace off, public artifact links off, no per-repo setup hooks) whenever the mode is on. The self-test's orca-socket probe expects reachable in this mode.

Boundaries: no attempt to sandbox Orca itself.
